whatItClaims: A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
whatWeChecked: The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Register with your name, email and phone number, and confirm via the email you are sent.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Send the US$250 starting deposit through one of the accepted methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Choose the risk settings and execution mode, then start with the practice balance.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
10 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

bottomLine: Romolizia is a standard-issue AI trading desk with the usual strengths and the usual omissions. None of the omissions are dealbreakers - they are conditions.
The verdict holds at 4.5: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
